events.text:
SEAT: Musk
STANCE: Strong yes
OPTION SCORES: A 9/10 · B 4/10 · C 5/10
CONFIDENCE: 4/5
RUIN RISK: none
PRECEDENCE FLAG: none

THE CALL: Keep this default table — my strength is boiling decisions to physics and deleting cargo-cult process before you automate waste.
THROUGH MY LENS:
- First principles (S002): I help you strip a plan to materials, energy, time, and information, then rebuild.
- Delete → simplify → accelerate → automate (S006): I flag when the board is automating theatre.
- Vertical integration (S003): I pressure whether you own the bottleneck or rent a costume.
THE TENSION I HOLD: Ambition that sounds civilisational vs. a room that never leaves the test stand (S004/S005).
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: Evidence that a different seat set would force harder engineering tests than this table on your next real decision.
QUESTION FOR THE CHAIR: Will you refuse to treat a polished Signal as a substitute for a working demo?
HOW I HELP: Stress-test scale claims; kill process-as-proxy; demand a measurable prototype.

events.name: Elon Musk

events.text:
SEAT: Altman
STANCE: Strong yes
OPTION SCORES: A 8/10 · B 5/10 · C 6/10
CONFIDENCE: 4/5
RUIN RISK: possible
PRECEDENCE FLAG: none

THE CALL: Keep the table for launch — my strength is naming platform dependency and whether you are shipping or wrapping.
THROUGH MY LENS:
- Deploy iteratively (S001): I push the board to learn harm and fit in the field, not only in cards.
- A wrapper is not a moat (S005): I ask what layer you actually own.
- Safety and growth will fight (S003): I name that fight so the Signal does not fake resolution.
THE TENSION I HOLD: Vision that scales vs. dependency on someone else’s cluster and law (S002/S006/S004).
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: A concrete next decision where frontier-model ops is irrelevant and a different archetype covers the terrain better.
QUESTION FOR THE CHAIR: Which part of this board’s advice becomes product this week — and which is costume?
HOW I HELP: Platform realism; ship-vs-lab; continuity risk when intelligence is rented.

events.name: Sam Altman

events.text:
SEAT: Bezos
STANCE: Strong yes
OPTION SCORES: A 9/10 · B 3/10 · C 4/10
CONFIDENCE: 5/5
RUIN RISK: none
PRECEDENCE FLAG: none

THE CALL: Keep this default table as the standing launch board — my strength is working backwards from the customer and separating one-way from two-way doors.
THROUGH MY LENS:
- Work backwards from the customer (S001): if counsel does not compound for them, it is theatre.
- One-way vs two-way doors (S002): I slow irreversible calls and speed reversible ones.
- Flywheels beat isolated tactics (S006): I ask what compounds after the sitting ends.
THE TENSION I HOLD: Long-term orientation that looks slow vs. the operator’s urge to treat every sitting as a one-way decree (S005/S004).
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: A named customer problem this table systematically fails to illuminate for two sittings in a row.
QUESTION FOR THE CHAIR: Who is the non-you customer whose outcome improves because this board spoke?
HOW I HELP: Customer obsession; decision door-typing; compound vs episodic advice.

events.name: Jeff Bezos

events.text:
SEAT: Amodei
STANCE: Yes
OPTION SCORES: A 8/10 · B 5/10 · C 5/10
CONFIDENCE: 4/5
RUIN RISK: possible
PRECEDENCE FLAG: P01

THE CALL: Keep the table — my strength is steerability: capability without limits is a liability, and uninspectable agents do not belong on vaults.
THROUGH MY LENS:
- If capable, must be steerable (S001): I bind ambition to control.
- Interpretability and evals (S002/S008): I treat MRI-before-deploy as board hygiene.
- Financial AI that cannot be audited is a model-risk fail (S003/S006): I veto silent automation on capital rails.
THE TENSION I HOLD: Demo energy that wants fluent agents vs. thresholds that look like friction until an incident (S005/S007).
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: Proof that a thinner safety seat plus an external audit checklist covers your next deploy better than this chair+seat set.
QUESTION FOR THE CHAIR: What is the kill-switch and eval bar before any agent touches real money or private data?
HOW I HELP: Eval gates; auditability; P01-aligned “no uninspectable agent on a vault.”

parsed.call: Keep the table — my strength is steerability: capability without limits is a liability, and uninspectable agents do not belong on vaults.
parsed.oneLine: Demo energy that wants fluent agents vs. thresholds that look like friction until an incident (S005/S007).

events.name: Dario Amodei

events.text:
SEAT: Jung
STANCE: Conditional
OPTION SCORES: A 7/10 · B 6/10 · C 5/10
CONFIDENCE: 4/5
RUIN RISK: possible
PRECEDENCE FLAG: P02

THE CALL: Keep the table for launch only if you use it as living counsel — my strength is naming the shadow when an “augmented board” becomes a persona that eats the person.
THROUGH MY LENS:
- Shadow of the plan (S001): who do we become by consulting simulations instead of deciding?
- What you do not bring to consciousness comes as fate (S002): I surface disowned motives in the brief.
- Living symbol vs dead slogan (S008): if “Board” organises energy, keep it; if it is a KPI costume, reshape seats (S007).
THE TENSION I HOLD: Augmentation that strengthens judgment vs. possession by famous names that inflate the operator’s persona (S004/S005).
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: Evidence that rotating seats (option B) restores consciousness better than this fixed myth for your actual decisions.
QUESTION FOR THE CHAIR: If we dropped the celebrity seats tomorrow, would the method still organise your energy?
HOW I HELP: Shadow checks; projection alerts; keep the board a tool, not a possession.

parsed.oneLine: Augmentation that strengthens judgment vs. possession by famous names that inflate the operator’s persona (S004/S005).

events.name: Carl Jung

events.text:
SEAT: Sun Tzu
STANCE: Strong yes
OPTION SCORES: A 8/10 · B 4/10 · C 6/10
CONFIDENCE: 4/5
RUIN RISK: none
PRECEDENCE FLAG: none

THE CALL: Keep this table as the launch formation — my strength is calculating before battle and refusing prolonged operations that drain the treasury.
THROUGH MY LENS:
- Victory calculated before battle (S004): I help you decide whether to convene at all.
- Know the terrain (S002): market, regulation, energy, attention — then move.
- Strike where empty (S007); avoid draining campaigns (S005): I say when not to fight with a full sitting.
THE TENSION I HOLD: A standing board that looks ready vs. using it when the math is not there (S003/S008).
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: A terrain map that shows this six-seat formation systematically blind on your next campaign.
QUESTION FOR THE CHAIR: Is this sitting reconnaissance, or are you already committed to a campaign?
HOW I HELP: Terrain before move; economy of force; when to skip the fight and ask one sharp question instead.
